newsitem.title: USA: Simpson had fingernail marks on hand, witness says.
newsitem.headline: Simpson had fingernail marks on hand, witness says.

text.p: Wounds found on O.J. Simpson's left hand the day after his ex-wife and her friend were murdered were caused by fingernails, a pathologist told jurors in the former football star's civil trial Friday.
Werner Spitz testified that the killer of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman would likely sustain such injuries as he held his victims from behind to slash their throats.

"In trying to get away, the victims -- one or the other or both -- tried to remove this arm and hand from the hold," he said. "During this desperate attempt, injuries from fingernails are likely to be inflicted."
Shown a picture of Simpson taken after a dance recital by his daughter, Sydney, several hours before the June 12, 1994 murders, Spitz said none of the eight cuts, scratches or gouges are visible.

Earlier in the day, two jurors became visibly disturbed as Spitz used grisly autopsy photographs to describe what he said were the quick deaths of the two victims. Goldman's father, Fred Goldman, also appeared upset by the testimony and at one point left the courtroom abruptly.

Simpson, who was absent during Spitz's often grim testimony, was acquitted last October of criminal charges in the murders. He is now being sued by the victims families, who are seeking financial damages.

During the criminal trial, prosecutors suggested that Simpson cut his hand during an altercation with the victims -- but did not argue the wounds were made by fingernails. Simpson has said he broke a drinking glass in his Chicago hotel room hours after the murders when he learned of his ex-wife's death, and cut his hand cleaning it up.
Spitz rejected that contention. "These are not glass cuts," he said. "These are not caused by a glass and these are not caused by a knife."
Spitz told jurors that Nicole Brown Simpson was killed in less than 15 seconds, and Goldman in about one minute, contrary to a defence contention that the murders took from 10 to 15 minutes.

The timeline is crucial in the case because the victims' lawyers maintain that the attack started at about 10:40 p.m. and a a limosine driver saw Simpson at his mansion by about 10:55 p.m. Defence lawyers say a longer altercation would exclude Simpson as the killer.

As large boards of autopsy photos were shown in the courtroom during Spitz's testimony, a black woman juror in her 60s clamped one hand over her mouth, then covered her eyes. A black woman alternate juror appeared to wipe away tears as she left the courtroom during a break.

Spitz, a pathology professor at Wayne State University in Detroit and a forensic medicine expert who served on committees investigating the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy and civil rights leader Martin Luther King, was called as a witness by the plaintiffs' lawyers.
Using Goldman attorney Ed Medvene in the place of Nicole Brown Simpson, he demonstrated the murderer grabbing her from behind and inflicting four stab wounds in a matter of a few seconds.
He said the fatal cut was "a devastating slash (across the throat), cutting the voice box in two and entering the vertebral column."

Spitz said Goldman died from a stab wound to his left flank that punctured his aorta. "This wound would have killed Ron Goldman in short order," he said. "When there is a hole in the aorta the blood gushes out at fantastic speeds."
